negative_control.family: AAO's own 8 bins (never pooled with the positive outcomes)

verdict.reading: R returns the same value for an anomaly placed BEFORE onset as for one placed AFTER it. A pre-onset anomaly has causal fraction zero by construction, so R is NOT an estimator of the causal fraction; it measures how tightly the anomaly is concentrated around the onset date. The original validation simulated only the post-onset structure and therefore could not detect this.

synthetic.equal_skill: outcome + N(0, 2500) per member + N(0, 2500) shared by the members of each (start, lead)
synthetic.ssw_skill: as equal_skill at SSW starts; elsewhere the ERA5 outcome of another year at the same calendar dates, plus the same noise

selection_law_enso.json.note: at the natural 92% rate the selection is nearly no selection and the bias is ~0 for every outcome, which is itself the contrast with SSW at 70%: a more consistent teleconnection leaves less room for outcome-based selection to bias anything

stratifier_bias_law.json.verdict: LAW HOLDS on observations: every stratifier's null residual contains zero, so beta x dS accounts for the whole non-causal contrast and the residual is an unbiased differential effect.

posthoc.label: post hoc, added after the registered result was seen

is_downward_propagation_a_class.json.verdict: NO CLASS in CMIP6_ensemble (n=1517): the per-event surface response is unimodal (dip p=0.8235), one Gaussian component suffices (BIC-gap p=0.9650), and the whole distribution is a pure SHIFT of -0.476 sigma of the ordinary winter distribution (KS p=0.3456). 'Downward propagation' is a threshold on a continuum, not a population.

era_dependence_gate.json.verdict: POOLING REFUSED. T1 passed, T2 3/7 betas agree. The observational arm stays at n=30 (1979 onward) and the pre-satellite extension is reported only as a sensitivity test, with the failing diagnostic stated.
era_dependence_gate.json.headline_recommendation: Pre-specified global rule REFUSES pooling, and that verdict stands as the headline: the observational arm is n=30. Per-stratifier, 6/7 survive both checks (vT_pre30, vT_pre15, u10_post30, u10_post45, z100_post, AO_post) and the n=42 record is reported for those as a pre-registered sensitivity test, never as the primary number.

excluded.NRL: nudged-minus-control ensemble effect identically zero (max |S| = 0.00781 Pa) -- corrupt submission

power_within_ensemble.note: Power to detect a WITHIN-ensemble correlation at n members. The 0.85 row is included only for scale: it is Loeffel's BETWEEN-EVENT value on ensemble means and is not the same estimand as anything measured here.

falsifier_primary.rule: R interval excludes 0 AND |R| > 0.2 sigma in NEURASIA

snapsi_selection_test.json.criterion: Karpechko et al. (2017) conditions 1 and 2 (the surface conditions) applied to nudged members whose stratospheric forcing is identical by design

excluded.NRL: |nudged - control| ensemble-mean effect is < 1 Pa at every initialisation (max 0.00781 Pa): corrupt submission, not a null result

paired_NH.note: residual = observed contrast minus the contrast a cut at zero gives on one Gaussian with the ensemble's own mean and sd; ~0 means one population suffices. Pairs exist only where BOTH arms have >=3 members per class, so the 11 nearly-all-DW nudged ensembles are absent from the paired test (they cannot form a contrast); the DW rate uses all ensembles.

southern_hemisphere.event: Austral MINOR warming, central date 2019-09-18 (SNAPSI protocol, Hitchcock et al. GMD 15, 5073, 2022)
southern_hemisphere.caveat: The 10 hPa 60S wind never reversed, so this is NOT an SSW under the WMO definition. It tests generality to a different hemisphere AND a weaker class of event. s20191001 initialises 13 days after the central date and cannot span the +8..+25 window, so only s20190829 contributes.

snapsi_selection_test.json.filter_caveat: The DW-NDW contrast requires >=3 members in BOTH groups, which is asymmetric by construction: only an arm with a strong forced shift can push nearly every member into one class. 11 of 36 nudged ensembles are dropped that way, with a mean DW rate of 0.993, while 0 of 36 control ensembles are. Quote mean_DW_rate_UNCONDITIONAL for the rate; the contrast is necessarily conditioned on the ensembles where both groups exist, which are the weaker-responding ones.
snapsi_selection_test.json.units_caveat: Contrasts here are standardised by the CONTROL ensemble's member-to-member spread for a single event. The published -0.708 is standardised by the BETWEEN-EVENT spread in observations. These are different yardsticks, so ratio_to_published indicates scale and is not an exact like-for-like fraction.

calibration_posthoc.label: post hoc, added after code review

era5_nam_daily_mean_check.json.question: does the January 2019 Karpechko 1000 hPa label survive a true daily-mean NAM?

era5_recompute_and_two_thirds.json.verdict: In ERA5 the published criterion gives a DW-minus-NDW contrast of -0.682 of which 97% is the selection term. A pure surface shift of -0.636 sigma applied to event-free dates gives a 75% pass rate against 69% observed -- so 'about two thirds propagate downward' is what ONE shifted population produces, with no classes in it.

test_B.interpretation: UPPER BOUND on the structural share only; their r is between ensemble means, which suppresses the noise driving this bias.

recompute_published_criterion.json.criterion: Karpechko et al. 2017 conditions 1-3 (condition 3 at 100 hPa, not 150)
recompute_published_criterion.json.verdict: The published criterion produces a DW-minus-NDW NAO contrast of -0.543; 88% of it is the selection term beta x dS. Residual -0.067 (p=0.495). For scale, ACP 26, 3723 (2026) publishes -0.708 from the same criterion.
